local_checks.result: Re-checked at a1f22eca (U311b on U311 0059848e on origin/main 2b2415f6): the only change since run-23's head replaces one README row (README.md:1230) with one row, so every file below is byte-identical to run-23's head and every line holds as run-23 read it; the lever is the 2b2415f6 lever (blob 38401bbf, sha256 5e1b92b2...), the code run-19 read. DEFAULT_ENV_NAMES gains OMP_PROFILE and nothing else (config.mjs:10-13), with the reason beside it (:3-9). The plugin spawns the child with pickEnv(config.env) (index.mjs:73), and pickEnv copies only listed names that exist in the plugin's own environment (gateway-client.mjs:26-33), so OMP_PROFILE reaches the child only when the launcher set it; under hcom-seat's dsh role that value is the lever's own OMP_PROFILE=dsh, set under env -i (hcom-seat:2268). The list still names no credential: the use-case test asserts no KEY, TOKEN, SECRET, OAUTH or PASSWORD name (test/use-cases.test.mjs:622-626), and the new recorder test asserts the child carries OMP_PROFILE when the plugin has it and not when it is unset, with a non-row name dropped (test/gateway-client.test.mjs:251-283). The value moves the child from ~/.omp/agent, which the dsh role denies, to ~/.omp/profiles/dsh, which the role already grants for read and write (hcom-seat:1494, :1795) and which the judge pins to its own position (:1801-1805); srt still denies every other profile, so a different value would fail as the g6 run did, not widen. The row's `env` can replace the list (config.mjs:37), but the profile file is the operator's managed file, and a value only ever comes from the plugin's own environment. Outside hcom-seat, an operator running dsh directly forwards their own OMP_PROFILE to their own child.

hardening_notes: With OMP_PROFILE=dsh the gateway child keeps its omp state, agent.db and whatever login state omp stores there, in ~/.omp/profiles/dsh, a dsh write root the contained session can read and rewrite (hcom-seat:1494, :1795). The child's environment carries no token name, so its Claude login is read from that profile or from a source this run may not inspect. If it is a stored refresh credential, it is a second copy of the operator's login inside the sandbox beside the CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN the shim exports (carried pattern), and it would outlive the launch. Not verified: the profile's contents are a credential store.

It fails closed, so this is an availability defect, not a widening; not verified on Linux. `local LC_ALL=C` in path_presence, as pointer_value does, would make the test locale-independent.

slots_remove runs on the normal exit and on HUP, INT and TERM, not on a refuse() inside seat_sandbox_write after the slots are made (the settings write :2145-2147, the shim install :2232-2234, the wrapper writes); an EXIT-scoped removal for the foreground role would leave nothing behind. The removal runs once the foreground child has ended, but a process the session started in the background may outlive dsh if srt does not end the sandbox's process tree (not verified on srt 0.0.81). Such a process still holds write access to the state slot and could race the operator's chmod -R and rm -rf traversal, for example by swapping a directory for a link mid-walk. Renaming the slot out of the write root first (into the write-denied .sandbox, say) and removing it there would close that window.

~/.omp/run is a write root of every seat, the dsh role included (hcom-seat:1494), and holds the omp session-owner locks and daemon records (session-owners/, daemons/) that the operator's own omp and the other seats read outside the dsh sandbox. A contained dsh session can therefore delete or rewrite them. With no unix socket and no local binding it cannot stand in for a daemon, so the reach is denial of service or lock confusion for other omp sessions; not verified. If the dsh role's login child needs no shared lease, a per-role run directory, or a dsh row without ~/.omp/run, would keep the session off the other seats' state.
